key_insight: Microscopic impurities seed perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can rapidly flag films at higher risk.
engineering_relevance: Fast, non-invasive impurity screening could support quality control for scalable, stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation sites.
Detect and quantify impurities within seconds using reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress tests linked degradation onset to impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density showed faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validation across different film compositions and manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
